algeria/adventure.caption: Crossing the Tassili
algeria/adventure.description: A week on foot with Tuareg guides among the sandstone towers, sleeping out.
algeria/adventure.alt: hikers among the sandstone towers of Tassili n'Ajjer, Algeria

algeria/architecture.caption: The Casbah and the M'zab
algeria/architecture.description: Ottoman houses on top of each other in Algiers, and five fortified towns in the M'zab built to one plan.
algeria/architecture.alt: the tiered houses and minaret of Ghardaia in the M'zab valley, Algeria

algeria/beaches.caption: A Thousand Kilometres of Mediterranean
algeria/beaches.description: The Turquoise Coast west of Algiers, and the coves at Jijel under limestone cliffs.
algeria/beaches.alt: a limestone cove on the Jijel coast with clear water, Algeria

algeria/cities.caption: Algiers, White on the Bay
algeria/cities.description: The Casbah stacked above the harbour, and the boulevards the French cut below it.
algeria/cities.alt: the white terraces of the Casbah of Algiers above the bay, Algeria

algeria/crafts.caption: Silver, Wool and Pottery
algeria/crafts.description: Kabyle silver with coral and enamel, Beni Isguen weaving, and the pottery of Maatkas.
algeria/crafts.alt: Kabyle silver jewellery with coral and enamel on a cloth, Algeria

algeria/culture.caption: Three Languages Before Lunch
algeria/culture.description: Darija, Tamazight and French, and a coastline that has been argued over for three thousand years.
algeria/culture.alt: a busy street in the Casbah of Algiers with people talking, Algeria

algeria/eco-tourism.caption: The Case for Going Now
algeria/eco-tourism.description: Algeria takes very few visitors for its size, and everything about it is the better for that.
algeria/eco-tourism.alt: an empty Roman street at Djemila with nobody on it, Algeria

algeria/family-community.caption: Beaches and Roman Stones
algeria/family-community.description: Tipaza has a Roman city on a beach, which solves most family arguments at once.
algeria/family-community.alt: Roman columns at Tipaza with the Mediterranean behind, Algeria

algeria/festivals.caption: Yennayer and the Sufi Moussems
algeria/festivals.description: The Amazigh new year in January, and the moussems that fill desert towns for a week.
algeria/festivals.alt: dancers at the Amazigh Yennayer new year celebration, Algeria

algeria/food.caption: Couscous on Friday
algeria/food.description: Chorba, m'hadjeb, and the Friday couscous that stops the whole country.
algeria/food.alt: a plate of Algerian couscous with vegetables and broth

algeria/forests.caption: The Kabylie Cedars
algeria/forests.description: Atlas cedar on the Djurdjura ridge, some of it four hundred years old.
algeria/forests.alt: ancient Atlas cedar trees on the Djurdjura ridge in Kabylie, Algeria

algeria/heritage.caption: Seven Sites, Nine Thousand Years
algeria/heritage.description: Tassili's rock art records a Sahara with rivers in it, and the M'zab valley is still lived in.
algeria/heritage.alt: prehistoric rock paintings of cattle at Tassili n'Ajjer, Algeria

algeria/hero.caption: The Sahara Begins Here
algeria/hero.description: Four-fifths of Algeria is desert, and the last fifth holds forty million people.
algeria/hero.alt: the dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental in southern Algeria at low sun

algeria/hidden-gems.caption: Ghardaia
algeria/hidden-gems.description: Five towns in a valley, built by the Mozabites in the eleventh century and still run their way.
algeria/hidden-gems.alt: the pyramid-stacked town of Ghardaia rising to its mosque, Algeria

algeria/historic-sites.caption: Timgad and Djemila
algeria/historic-sites.description: Two Roman cities the desert kept: Timgad's grid is complete, Djemila's forum still stands.
algeria/historic-sites.alt: the Roman ruins and triumphal arch of Timgad on the high plateau, Algeria

algeria/lakes-rivers.caption: Chotts and Oases
algeria/lakes-rivers.description: Salt lakes that mirror the sky at Chott Melrhir, and the palmeraie at Timimoun.
algeria/lakes-rivers.alt: the palm oasis and red ksar walls of Timimoun in the Gourara, Algeria

algeria/local-life.caption: Coffee and Argument
algeria/local-life.description: The cafe is the institution. So is the argument in it.
algeria/local-life.alt: men at a pavement cafe table in Algiers talking, Algeria

algeria/luxury.caption: Rare, and Getting Less So
algeria/luxury.description: Restored Ottoman houses in the Casbah, and desert camps in the Hoggar run to a standard.
algeria/luxury.alt: a restored Ottoman courtyard house in the Casbah of Algiers, Algeria

algeria/mountains.caption: The Djurdjura and the Hoggar
algeria/mountains.description: Snow on the Djurdjura above Kabylie in winter; Mount Tahat at 2,908 metres in the far south.
algeria/mountains.alt: snow on the Djurdjura range above the Kabylie valleys, Algeria

algeria/nature.caption: Hoggar and Tassili
algeria/nature.description: Volcanic spires in the Hoggar, and a sandstone plateau at Tassili n'Ajjer eroded into streets.
algeria/nature.alt: the volcanic pinnacles of the Hoggar massif near Tamanrasset, Algeria

algeria/outdoor.caption: Walking the North
algeria/outdoor.description: The Chrea forest above Blida, the Gouraya cliffs at Bejaia, and the Djurdjura ridge.
algeria/outdoor.alt: a walking path along the Gouraya cliffs above Bejaia, Algeria

algeria/photography.caption: Light on Sandstone
algeria/photography.description: Tassili at either end of the day, when the rock goes from ochre to red to purple.
algeria/photography.alt: sandstone formations at Tassili n'Ajjer in late afternoon light, Algeria

algeria/safari.caption: Desert Watching, Not Game Driving
algeria/safari.description: There is no safari circuit here. You go out at dawn with somebody who reads tracks.
algeria/safari.alt: a guide reading animal tracks in sand in the Algerian Sahara

algeria/traditional-people.caption: The Kabyles and the Tuareg
algeria/traditional-people.description: Berber-speaking Kabylie in the north, and the Tuareg of the Hoggar in the far south.
algeria/traditional-people.alt: a Tuareg man in indigo tagelmust in the Hoggar, Algeria

algeria/waterfalls.caption: Water in a Dry Country
algeria/waterfalls.description: The falls at Kefrida in Bejaia, in a green fold of the coast that surprises everyone.
algeria/waterfalls.alt: the Kefrida waterfall falling through green forest in Bejaia province, Algeria

algeria/why-visit.caption: Why Algeria
algeria/why-visit.description: The Roman cities of Tunisia, the Sahara of Libya and the Atlas of Morocco, with almost nobody in them.
algeria/why-visit.alt: a lone traveller looking out over the Grand Erg from a dune, Algeria

algeria/wildlife.caption: What Lives in the Sand
algeria/wildlife.description: Fennec fox, addax and the last Saharan cheetah, all of them nocturnal and all of them rare.
algeria/wildlife.alt: a fennec fox at the edge of dunes in the Algerian Sahara

angola/adventure.caption: The Southern Desert
angola/adventure.description: Iona, the Tundavala gap and the escarpment road down to Namibe.
angola/adventure.alt: the sheer escarpment and drop at the Tundavala gap, Angola

angola/architecture.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Modernist
angola/architecture.description: Fortaleza de Sao Miguel, Benguela's pastel streets, and Luanda's late-modernist blocks.
angola/architecture.alt: the yellow walls of the Fortaleza de Sao Miguel above Luanda, Angola

angola/beaches.caption: Sixteen Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
angola/beaches.description: The Ilha at Luanda, the Mussulo lagoon, and the dune coast running south to Iona.
angola/beaches.alt: the sand spit of the Ilha do Cabo curving across Luanda bay, Angola

angola/cities.caption: Luanda and Benguela
angola/cities.description: A bay closed by a sand spit and a skyline that went up fast, and a quieter colonial port south.
angola/cities.alt: Luanda's high-rise skyline curving round the bay, Angola

angola/crafts.caption: The Pensador and Basketry
angola/crafts.description: The Chokwe Thinker is the national symbol, and Chokwe masks and chairs are among Africa's finest.
angola/crafts.alt: a carved Chokwe Thinker figure in dark wood, Angola

angola/culture.caption: Semba, Kizomba and Kuduro
angola/culture.description: Semba became samba across the Atlantic, and kuduro went back the other way.
angola/culture.alt: dancers and a sound system at a kuduro party in Luanda, Angola

angola/eco-tourism.caption: Bringing the Sable Back
angola/eco-tourism.description: The giant sable was found alive in 2004 and has been fenced, guarded and bred since.
angola/eco-tourism.alt: a ranger monitoring giant sable in a fenced sanctuary, Angola

angola/family-community.caption: The Mussulo
angola/family-community.description: A lagoon behind the spit south of Luanda, calm, shallow and full of families at weekends.
angola/family-community.alt: families in shallow lagoon water at the Mussulo, Angola

angola/festivals.caption: Carnaval da Vitoria
angola/festivals.description: Luanda's carnival on the Marginal, with the neighbourhood groups competing.
angola/festivals.alt: carnival dancers in costume on Luanda's Marginal, Angola

angola/food.caption: Funge, Muamba and Calulu
angola/food.description: Funge with muamba de galinha, calulu with dried fish, and Portuguese pastries after.
angola/food.alt: a plate of muamba de galinha with funge, Angola

angola/forests.caption: Maiombe
angola/forests.description: Angola's Amazon — rainforest in the Cabinda exclave, north of the Congo river.
angola/forests.alt: dense rainforest canopy in the Maiombe forest of Cabinda, Angola

angola/heritage.caption: Mbanza Kongo, Listed
angola/heritage.description: Inscribed in 2017 as the seat of a kingdom that dealt with Portugal as an equal.
angola/heritage.alt: the archaeological site and old walls at Mbanza Kongo, Angola

angola/hero.caption: Kalandula
angola/hero.description: A hundred and five metres of water across four hundred, in the middle of nowhere.
angola/hero.alt: the wide curtain of the Kalandula falls in Malanje, Angola

angola/hidden-gems.caption: Tundavala
angola/hidden-gems.description: A gap in the escarpment where the ground drops a thousand metres, with no railing.
angola/hidden-gems.alt: a figure at the edge of the Tundavala gap looking down, Angola

angola/historic-sites.caption: Mbanza Kongo
angola/historic-sites.description: The capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, and the first sub-Saharan city to have a stone cathedral.
angola/historic-sites.alt: the ruined stone cathedral walls at Mbanza Kongo, Angola

angola/lakes-rivers.caption: The Kwanza and the Cunene
angola/lakes-rivers.description: The Kwanza runs to the Atlantic below Luanda; the Cunene is the Namibian border.
angola/lakes-rivers.alt: the wide Kwanza river running to the Atlantic, Angola

angola/local-life.caption: The Marginal at Six
angola/local-life.description: The whole city walks and runs the bay road in the evening, and keeps doing it after dark.
angola/local-life.alt: people walking and running the Marginal in Luanda at dusk, Angola

angola/luxury.caption: Luanda, and Little Else
angola/luxury.description: Good hotels in the capital, and very little organised outside it.
angola/luxury.alt: a hotel terrace looking over Luanda bay at sunset, Angola

angola/mountains.caption: Mount Moco
angola/mountains.description: 2,620 metres in the Huambo highlands, with the last Afromontane forest in the country on it.
angola/mountains.alt: the grassy summit of Mount Moco above patches of forest, Angola

angola/nature.caption: The Black Rocks and the Namib
angola/nature.description: Pungo Andongo's monoliths in the north, and the Namib running the whole southern coast.
angola/nature.alt: the black monoliths of Pungo Andongo standing over grassland, Angola

angola/outdoor.caption: The Escarpment Roads
angola/outdoor.description: Serra da Leba's hairpins, and Tundavala where the plateau simply stops.
angola/outdoor.alt: the hairpin bends of the Serra da Leba pass from above, Angola

angola/photography.caption: Water and Rock
angola/photography.description: Kalandula in the wet season, when the spray reaches the viewpoint.
angola/photography.alt: spray rising from the Kalandula falls in full flow, Angola

angola/safari.caption: Kissama and Luengue-Luiana
angola/safari.description: Kissama two hours from Luanda, restocked and recovering; the southeast on the Okavango's headwaters.
angola/safari.alt: elephants in open woodland in Kissama National Park, Angola

angola/traditional-people.caption: Ovimbundu, Mbundu, Bakongo, Ovahimba
angola/traditional-people.description: Ovimbundu in the centre, Bakongo in the north, and Ovahimba along the Cunene.
angola/traditional-people.alt: an Ovahimba woman in ochre and braided hair near the Cunene, Angola

angola/waterfalls.caption: Kalandula and Ruacana
angola/waterfalls.description: Kalandula in Malanje, and the Ruacana falls on the Cunene where Namibia begins.
angola/waterfalls.alt: water thundering over the Ruacana falls on the Cunene, Angola

angola/why-visit.caption: Why Angola
angola/why-visit.description: A waterfall to rival Victoria's, a desert coast, and a capital that surprises everyone.
angola/why-visit.alt: the Kalandula falls with nobody at the viewpoint, Angola

angola/wildlife.caption: Giant Sable
angola/wildlife.description: The palanca negra gigante lives in Angola and nowhere else, and was thought extinct until 2004.
angola/wildlife.alt: a giant sable antelope with long curved horns in miombo woodland, Angola

benin/adventure.caption: Pirogue and Pendjari
benin/adventure.description: Poling through Ganvie in the morning, and a game drive in the north two days later.
benin/adventure.alt: a pirogue being poled between stilt houses at Ganvie, Benin

benin/architecture.caption: Earth and Afro-Brazilian
benin/architecture.description: Somba tata towers in the north, and Afro-Brazilian merchant houses in Ouidah and Porto-Novo.
benin/architecture.alt: an Afro-Brazilian merchant house with shuttered windows in Porto-Novo, Benin

benin/beaches.caption: A Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
benin/beaches.description: Grand-Popo and Ouidah, with heavy surf and coconut palms right down to the sand.
benin/beaches.alt: palms and heavy Atlantic surf on the beach at Grand-Popo, Benin

benin/cities.caption: Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Abomey
benin/cities.description: A port that never stops, a colonial capital, and the seat of a kingdom.
benin/cities.alt: the Dantokpa market and motorcycle taxis in Cotonou, Benin

benin/crafts.caption: Applique and Bronze
benin/crafts.description: The Abomey applique banners that recorded the kings' reigns, and Fon bronze casting.
benin/crafts.alt: an Abomey applique cloth banner with royal symbols, Benin

benin/culture.caption: Where Vodun Comes From
benin/culture.description: Not a folk survival — a living religion with millions of followers, and a public holiday.
benin/culture.alt: a vodun ceremony with drumming and white-clad participants, Benin

benin/eco-tourism.caption: Pendjari, Community-Run
benin/eco-tourism.description: Managed since 2017 by African Parks with the villages around it, and the lion count is up.
benin/eco-tourism.alt: a ranger scanning grassland from a vehicle in Pendjari, Benin

benin/family-community.caption: Ganvie by Pirogue
benin/family-community.description: A whole town on water, reached by boat, which no child has ever found boring.
benin/family-community.alt: children in a pirogue among the stilt houses of Ganvie, Benin

benin/festivals.caption: The Vodun Festival
benin/festivals.description: 10 January at Ouidah, on the beach, and it is a religious event before it is a spectacle.
benin/festivals.alt: crowds and dancers on the beach at the Ouidah vodun festival, Benin

benin/food.caption: Amiwo and Grilled Fish
benin/food.description: Amiwo — maize with tomato and chicken — and fish straight off the Grand-Popo beach.
benin/food.alt: a plate of amiwo with grilled chicken and pepper sauce, Benin

benin/forests.caption: The Sacred Forests
benin/forests.description: Kpasse at Ouidah and the groves around it, protected because they are vodun sites.
benin/forests.alt: tall trees and a shrine in the sacred forest of Kpasse at Ouidah, Benin

benin/heritage.caption: The Route of the Slaves
benin/heritage.description: Four kilometres from Ouidah's auction square to the Door of No Return on the beach.
benin/heritage.alt: the Door of No Return arch on the beach at Ouidah, Benin

benin/hero.caption: Ganvie
benin/hero.description: Thirty thousand people living on stilts in Lake Nokoue, moving between houses by pirogue.
benin/hero.alt: stilt houses and pirogues in the lake village of Ganvie, Benin

benin/hidden-gems.caption: Possotome and Lake Aheme
benin/hidden-gems.description: A quiet lake west of Ouidah with fishing villages and hot springs on its shore.
benin/hidden-gems.alt: fishing boats on the shore of Lake Aheme at Possotome, Benin

benin/historic-sites.caption: The Royal Palaces of Abomey
benin/historic-sites.description: Twelve palaces of the kings of Dahomey, in earth, with bas-reliefs telling the history.
benin/historic-sites.alt: earthen bas-reliefs on a wall of the royal palaces of Abomey, Benin

benin/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Nokoue and the Oueme
benin/lakes-rivers.description: The lagoon behind Cotonou, and the Oueme running down to it through the delta.
benin/lakes-rivers.alt: fishing nets and stakes across Lake Nokoue at dawn, Benin

benin/local-life.caption: Zemidjan
benin/local-life.description: The motorcycle taxis are the transport system, and their yellow shirts are the uniform.
benin/local-life.alt: yellow-shirted zemidjan motorcycle taxi riders waiting at a junction, Benin

benin/luxury.caption: A Few Good Ones
benin/luxury.description: Lodges at Pendjari and on the coast at Grand-Popo, and good hotels in Cotonou.
benin/luxury.alt: a beach lodge terrace among palms at Grand-Popo, Benin

benin/mountains.caption: The Atakora Range
benin/mountains.description: Six hundred metres of quartzite ridge in the northwest, with the Somba country under it.
benin/mountains.alt: the quartzite ridges of the Atakora range in northern Benin

benin/nature.caption: Pendjari and the Atakora
benin/nature.description: The Atakora hills in the northwest, and the Pendjari river running along the park.
benin/nature.alt: the Pendjari river running below wooded hills in the Atakora, Benin

benin/outdoor.caption: Walking the Atakora
benin/outdoor.description: Somba villages, quartzite ridges and the Tanougou pool, on foot from Natitingou.
benin/outdoor.alt: a footpath through Atakora hills past a Somba compound, Benin

benin/photography.caption: Stilts and Reflection
benin/photography.description: Ganvie at first light, when the water is still and the houses double.
benin/photography.alt: stilt houses reflected in still water at dawn in Ganvie, Benin

benin/safari.caption: The W-Arly-Pendjari Complex
benin/safari.description: The largest intact ecosystem in West Africa, run across three countries.
benin/safari.alt: elephants at a waterhole in Pendjari at the end of the dry season, Benin

benin/traditional-people.caption: Fon, Yoruba, Bariba, Somba
benin/traditional-people.description: The Fon of Dahomey in the south, the Somba in the Atakora with their fortified houses.
benin/traditional-people.alt: a Somba tata fortified mud house in the Atakora, Benin

benin/waterfalls.caption: Tanougou
benin/waterfalls.description: Falls off the Atakora into a deep pool, swimmable and cold.
benin/waterfalls.alt: the Tanougou waterfall falling into a green pool, Benin

benin/why-visit.caption: Why Benin
benin/why-visit.description: Vodun at its source, the palaces of Dahomey, and West Africa's best-run national park.
benin/why-visit.alt: a vodun devotee in white before a shrine at Ouidah, Benin

benin/wildlife.caption: Pendjari
benin/wildlife.description: Lion, elephant, buffalo and cheetah in one of the last strongholds of the West African lion.
benin/wildlife.alt: a West African lion in tall grass in Pendjari National Park, Benin
benin/wildlife.query: Benin West African Pendjari National Park

botswana/adventure.caption: Mokoro, Walking, Horseback
botswana/adventure.description: Poled canoes, walking safaris on the islands, and some of the best riding safaris anywhere.
botswana/adventure.alt: riders crossing a floodplain on a horseback safari, Botswana

botswana/architecture.caption: Tent, Deck and Sand
botswana/architecture.description: Camps built on decks above the flood, taken down when the concession lease ends.
botswana/architecture.alt: a tented camp on a deck above the Okavango floodplain, Botswana

botswana/beaches.caption: Landlocked
botswana/beaches.description: The nearest sea is a thousand kilometres away, and nobody here seems to mind.
botswana/beaches.alt: a floodplain island in the Okavango at sunrise, Botswana

botswana/cities.caption: Maun and Kasane
botswana/cities.description: Not really cities — two safari towns with airstrips, which is what the country needs.
botswana/cities.alt: light aircraft on the apron at Maun airport, Botswana

botswana/crafts.caption: Basketry
botswana/crafts.description: Palm baskets woven in the delta panhandle, dyed with bark, and collected worldwide.
botswana/crafts.alt: woven palm baskets from the Okavango panhandle, Botswana

botswana/culture.caption: Batswana and San
botswana/culture.description: Setswana across the country, and San communities in the Kalahari with the oldest culture on earth.
botswana/culture.alt: a San tracker reading spoor in the Kalahari sand, Botswana

botswana/eco-tourism.caption: Community Trusts
botswana/eco-tourism.description: Concessions leased through community trusts, so the villages hold the lease and the income.
botswana/eco-tourism.alt: a community conservation sign at a delta concession, Botswana

botswana/family-community.caption: Not the Cheapest, but Quiet
botswana/family-community.description: Not a budget destination — but the children will not be sharing a sighting with ten vehicles.
botswana/family-community.alt: a family on a mokoro in the Okavango channels, Botswana

botswana/festivals.caption: Maitisong and Dithubaruba
botswana/festivals.description: The Maitisong festival in Gaborone, and the Kweneng cultural festival at Dithubaruba.
botswana/festivals.alt: dancers performing at a cultural festival in Botswana

botswana/food.caption: Seswaa and Bogobe
botswana/food.description: Slow-pounded beef and sorghum porridge, and braai wherever there is a fire.
botswana/food.alt: seswaa and bogobe served at a Botswana lodge

botswana/forests.caption: Riverine and Mopane
botswana/forests.description: Riverine forest along the Chobe, and mopane woodland across the north.
botswana/forests.alt: riverine forest along the Chobe river bank, Botswana

botswana/heritage.caption: Diamonds and Democracy
botswana/heritage.description: Independent since 1966, and the one African country that used its diamonds well.
botswana/heritage.alt: the National Museum building in Gaborone, Botswana

botswana/hero.caption: A Delta That Never Reaches the Sea
botswana/hero.description: The Okavango floods into the Kalahari every year and simply disappears into it.
botswana/hero.alt: the channels and islands of the Okavango delta from the air, Botswana

botswana/hidden-gems.caption: The Makgadikgadi
botswana/hidden-gems.description: Drive onto the pan at night and there is no horizon and no sound at all.
botswana/hidden-gems.alt: quad bikes on the Makgadikgadi salt pan at dusk, Botswana

botswana/historic-sites.caption: Tsodilo Hills
botswana/historic-sites.description: Four thousand paintings on four hills the San call the resting place of the gods.
botswana/historic-sites.alt: rock paintings on the Tsodilo hills, Botswana

botswana/lakes-rivers.caption: The Okavango and the Chobe
botswana/lakes-rivers.description: A mokoro poled through papyrus channels is the correct speed for this country.
botswana/lakes-rivers.alt: a mokoro being poled through a papyrus channel, Botswana

botswana/local-life.caption: Cattle Posts
botswana/local-life.description: Away from the parks the country is cattle, and the cattle post is the centre of it.
botswana/local-life.alt: a cattle post at the edge of the Kalahari, Botswana

botswana/luxury.caption: The Concession Camps
botswana/luxury.description: Private concessions the size of small countries, with six tents on them.
botswana/luxury.alt: a small luxury tented camp lit at dusk in the delta, Botswana

botswana/mountains.caption: Tsodilo
botswana/mountains.description: No real mountains — Tsodilo's four hills hold four thousand rock paintings instead.
botswana/mountains.alt: the Tsodilo hills rising from flat Kalahari scrub, Botswana

botswana/nature.caption: Delta, Pan and Desert
botswana/nature.description: Water in the north, salt pans in the middle, and Kalahari sand for the rest of it.
botswana/nature.alt: the Makgadikgadi salt pans stretching to the horizon, Botswana

botswana/outdoor.caption: Mokoro and Walking
botswana/outdoor.description: Poling, walking and riding — this is the country where you get out of the vehicle.
botswana/outdoor.alt: walkers following a guide across an Okavango island, Botswana

botswana/photography.caption: Water and Light
botswana/photography.description: Aerial work over the delta, and reflections that only exist for the weeks of the flood.
botswana/photography.alt: aerial view of flooded Okavango channels at golden hour, Botswana

botswana/safari.caption: Low Volume, High Value
botswana/safari.description: Fewer beds, larger concessions, and game drives that do not meet another vehicle.
botswana/safari.alt: a game vehicle alone on a track in the Okavango, Botswana

botswana/traditional-people.caption: The Kalahari San
botswana/traditional-people.description: Tracking with San guides, who will find in an hour what nobody else sees at all.
botswana/traditional-people.alt: San guides walking a Kalahari pan in the morning, Botswana

botswana/waterfalls.caption: No Falls, and the Zambezi Next Door
botswana/waterfalls.description: The water here spreads rather than drops; Victoria Falls is ninety minutes from Kasane.
botswana/waterfalls.alt: the Chobe river spreading wide at sunset, Botswana

botswana/why-visit.caption: Fewer People Than Elephants
botswana/why-visit.description: Two and a half million people, a hundred and thirty thousand elephant, and space for both.
botswana/why-visit.alt: an elephant herd crossing open Kalahari grassland, Botswana

botswana/wildlife.caption: The Largest Elephant Population
botswana/wildlife.description: Chobe holds more elephant than anywhere on earth, and they come to the river at four.
botswana/wildlife.alt: elephants coming down to the Chobe river in late light, Botswana

burkina-faso/adventure.caption: Cycling the Southwest
burkina-faso/adventure.description: Burkina is a cycling nation. The Tour du Faso runs every year and the roads are flat.
burkina-faso/adventure.alt: cyclists on a red laterite road through savanna, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/architecture.caption: Sudanese Mud and Sukhala
burkina-faso/architecture.description: The Bobo-Dioulasso mosque in Sudanese style, and painted Kassena compounds at Tiebele.
burkina-faso/architecture.alt: the painted geometric walls of a Kassena compound at Tiebele, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/beaches.caption: Lakeshore, Not Coast
burkina-faso/beaches.description: Landlocked. Tengrela and the Bagre reservoir are where people swim and fish.
burkina-faso/beaches.alt: a fishing pirogue on Lake Tengrela at dusk, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/cities.caption: Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso
burkina-faso/cities.description: A capital that fills for FESPACO, and a second city with the country's best music.
burkina-faso/cities.alt: the mud-brick Grande Mosquee of Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/crafts.caption: Bronze and Masks
burkina-faso/crafts.description: Lost-wax bronze in Ouagadougou, and the plank masks of the Bwa and Nuna.
burkina-faso/crafts.alt: a tall painted Bwa plank mask with geometric patterns, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/culture.caption: Sixty Languages, One Cinema
burkina-faso/culture.description: FESPACO in Ouagadougou every two years, and a film industry that punches far above its size.
burkina-faso/culture.alt: a crowd outside a cinema at FESPACO in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/family-community.caption: Elephants You Can Walk To
burkina-faso/family-community.description: Nazinga allows walking safaris, which makes it unusually good for older children.
burkina-faso/family-community.alt: a family walking with a guide towards elephants at Nazinga, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/festivals.caption: FESPACO and FESTIMA
burkina-faso/festivals.description: The film festival in Ouagadougou, and the mask festival at Dedougou every other year.
burkina-faso/festivals.alt: masked dancers performing at the FESTIMA mask festival, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/food.caption: To and Riz Gras
burkina-faso/food.description: To — millet paste with sauce — and riz gras cooked in tomato and oil.
burkina-faso/food.alt: a bowl of to with green sauce beside a plate of riz gras, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/forests.caption: Gallery Forest at Banfora
burkina-faso/forests.description: The dome-shaped Sindou woodland, and the fields of sugarcane below the cliffs.
burkina-faso/forests.alt: gallery forest along a stream below the Banfora escarpment, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/heritage.caption: Loropeni, and the Living Rest
burkina-faso/heritage.description: One World Heritage site in stone, and a mask tradition that never became a museum.
burkina-faso/heritage.alt: a village mask performance with drummers and a crowd, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/hero.caption: The Sindou Peaks
burkina-faso/hero.description: A ridge of sandstone eroded into fins and needles, near Banfora in the southwest.
burkina-faso/hero.alt: the eroded sandstone fins and needles of the Sindou peaks, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/hidden-gems.caption: Tiebele
burkina-faso/hidden-gems.description: Kassena compounds painted in black, white and ochre geometry by the women of the household.
burkina-faso/hidden-gems.alt: women painting geometric patterns on a Kassena wall at Tiebele, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/historic-sites.caption: The Ruins of Loropeni
burkina-faso/historic-sites.description: Stone walls six metres high, a thousand years old, from the trans-Saharan gold trade.
burkina-faso/historic-sites.alt: the high laterite stone walls of the Loropeni ruins, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/lakes-rivers.caption: The Black and White Volta
burkina-faso/lakes-rivers.description: Two of the three Voltas rise here and run south into Ghana.
burkina-faso/lakes-rivers.alt: the Black Volta river running between wooded banks, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/local-life.caption: The Maquis at Night
burkina-faso/local-life.description: Open-air bars with grilled chicken and dolo, and a band more often than not.
burkina-faso/local-life.alt: an open-air maquis at night with grilled food and a band, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/luxury.caption: Modest
burkina-faso/luxury.description: Good hotels in Ouagadougou and Bobo, and a lodge or two near Banfora.
burkina-faso/luxury.alt: a garden courtyard hotel in Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/mountains.caption: Tenakourou
burkina-faso/mountains.description: 747 metres in the southwest, and the highest ground in a country that is mostly plateau.
burkina-faso/mountains.alt: the sandstone escarpment of the southwest rising above farmland, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/nature.caption: The Southwest
burkina-faso/nature.description: Cascades, sugarcane and the Karfiguela falls where the land drops off the plateau.
burkina-faso/nature.alt: the Karfiguela cascades falling over rock ledges near Banfora, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/outdoor.caption: The Sindou Ridge
burkina-faso/outdoor.description: Scrambling routes through the fins, best in the last two hours of light.
burkina-faso/outdoor.alt: a walker among the sandstone fins of Sindou at sunset, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/photography.caption: Masks in Motion
burkina-faso/photography.description: FESTIMA, where the masks are danced rather than displayed and the dust is part of it.
burkina-faso/photography.alt: a masked dancer spinning in dust at a mask festival, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/safari.caption: Nazinga and Arli
burkina-faso/safari.description: Nazinga has one of the densest elephant populations in West Africa and you can walk in it.
burkina-faso/safari.alt: elephants at a waterhole in Nazinga ranch, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/traditional-people.caption: Mossi, Bobo, Lobi, Fulani
burkina-faso/traditional-people.description: The Mossi kingdoms in the centre, the Bobo and Lobi in the west, the Fulani across the north.
burkina-faso/traditional-people.alt: a Lobi compound with mud walls and a granary, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/waterfalls.caption: Karfiguela
burkina-faso/waterfalls.description: Water off the plateau in a series of ledges, swimmable at the bottom.
burkina-faso/waterfalls.alt: people swimming below the Karfiguela waterfall, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/why-visit.caption: Why Burkina Faso
burkina-faso/why-visit.description: The masks, the music and the cinema, in a country that has never traded on scenery.
burkina-faso/why-visit.alt: a crowd watching a masked performance in a village square, Burkina Faso

burkina-faso/wildlife.caption: Hippos at Tengrela
burkina-faso/wildlife.description: A lake outside Banfora with a resident hippo pod, worked by fishermen in pirogues.
burkina-faso/wildlife.alt: hippos surfacing in Lake Tengrela with a pirogue nearby, Burkina Faso

burundi/adventure.caption: Walking the Divide
burundi/adventure.description: Kibira on foot, Mount Heha in a morning, and the lake shore road south.
burundi/adventure.alt: a forest path along the ridge at Kibira, Burundi

burundi/architecture.caption: Colonial and Hillside
burundi/architecture.description: German and Belgian colonial in Bujumbura, and tiled hillside houses everywhere else.
burundi/architecture.alt: a Belgian colonial building in central Bujumbura, Burundi

burundi/beaches.caption: Saga and Karera Beaches
burundi/beaches.description: White sand on Tanganyika south of Bujumbura, with the Congo visible across the water.
burundi/beaches.alt: white sand and palms on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, Burundi

burundi/cities.caption: Bujumbura and Gitega
burundi/cities.description: A lakeside city with a long promenade, and the political capital up in the hills.
burundi/cities.alt: the lakefront and hills at Bujumbura, Burundi

burundi/crafts.caption: Basketry and Drums
burundi/crafts.description: Coiled agaseke baskets with pointed lids, and the drums themselves.
burundi/crafts.alt: coiled agaseke baskets with conical lids, Burundi

burundi/culture.caption: The Drums
burundi/culture.description: The royal drummers of Gishora are on the UNESCO list, and they are not a performance troupe.
burundi/culture.alt: Burundian royal drummers with drums on their heads

burundi/eco-tourism.caption: Kibira's Water
burundi/eco-tourism.description: The forest feeds the hydro that runs most of the country, and protecting it is not sentiment.
burundi/eco-tourism.alt: a clear stream running out of Kibira forest, Burundi

burundi/family-community.caption: Lake and Hills
burundi/family-community.description: Short distances, calm fresh water, and hippos to keep an eye on.
burundi/family-community.alt: children playing on the sand at a Lake Tanganyika beach, Burundi

burundi/festivals.caption: Gishora
burundi/festivals.description: The drum sanctuary above Gitega, where the drums are kept and danced on their own ground.
burundi/festivals.alt: drummers performing at the Gishora drum sanctuary, Burundi

burundi/food.caption: Beans, Ugali and Mukeke
burundi/food.description: Beans and plantain, ugali, and mukeke — a Tanganyika fish grilled on the beach.
burundi/food.alt: grilled mukeke fish with plantain on a plate, Burundi

burundi/forests.caption: Kibira
burundi/forests.description: Forty thousand hectares of montane forest on the divide, and the country's water tower.
burundi/forests.alt: mossy montane forest and tree ferns at Kibira, Burundi

burundi/heritage.caption: The Ritual Dance of the Royal Drum
burundi/heritage.description: Inscribed in 2014 — the drums, the dance and the making of them, together.
burundi/heritage.alt: a drum being carved and stretched at a Burundian workshop

burundi/hero.caption: Hills and Lake
burundi/hero.description: Every horizon is a ridge, and Tanganyika is at the bottom of all of them.
burundi/hero.alt: terraced green hills running down towards Lake Tanganyika, Burundi

burundi/hidden-gems.caption: Rusizi Delta
burundi/hidden-gems.description: Hippos, birds and the Congo across the water, twenty minutes from the capital.
burundi/hidden-gems.alt: hippos and birds in the Rusizi delta at dusk, Burundi

burundi/historic-sites.caption: Rutovu
burundi/historic-sites.description: A stone pyramid on a ridge marking the southernmost source of the Nile.
burundi/historic-sites.alt: the stone pyramid marking the Nile source at Rutovu, Burundi

burundi/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Tanganyika
burundi/lakes-rivers.description: The second deepest lake on earth, and Burundi has a hundred and sixty kilometres of it.
burundi/lakes-rivers.alt: the deep blue water of Lake Tanganyika from a hillside, Burundi

burundi/local-life.caption: The Beach on a Sunday
burundi/local-life.description: Bujumbura goes to Saga beach, and stays until the light goes.
burundi/local-life.alt: crowds at Saga beach on Lake Tanganyika on a Sunday, Burundi

burundi/luxury.caption: Modest
burundi/luxury.description: A handful of hotels in Bujumbura, and lodges on the lake shore.
burundi/luxury.alt: a lakeside hotel terrace at Bujumbura, Burundi

burundi/mountains.caption: Mount Heha
burundi/mountains.description: 2,684 metres, an hour from the capital, with the whole rift visible from the top.
burundi/mountains.alt: the view from Mount Heha across ridges towards Lake Tanganyika, Burundi

burundi/nature.caption: The Congo-Nile Divide
burundi/nature.description: A ridge running the length of the country, with the Nile on one side and the Congo on the other.
burundi/nature.alt: the forested ridge of the Congo-Nile divide under cloud, Burundi

burundi/outdoor.caption: Hiking the Hills
burundi/outdoor.description: Heha, Kibira and the ridge roads, none of them more than a day.
burundi/outdoor.alt: a walker on a ridge path above terraced hills, Burundi

burundi/photography.caption: Drums in Motion
burundi/photography.description: Gishora mid-performance, when the drums are carried and struck at once.
burundi/photography.alt: a Burundian drummer leaping with a drum in performance

burundi/safari.caption: Rusizi and Ruvubu
burundi/safari.description: Hippo and crocodile in the Rusizi delta, and buffalo and antelope along the Ruvubu.
burundi/safari.alt: hippos in the Rusizi river delta near Bujumbura, Burundi

burundi/traditional-people.caption: Hutu, Tutsi and Twa
burundi/traditional-people.description: One language, Kirundi, spoken by everybody, and a history the country is still working through.
burundi/traditional-people.alt: a village gathering under a tree in the Burundian hills

burundi/waterfalls.caption: Karera
burundi/waterfalls.description: Four falls in one forested gorge in the southeast, with a path between them.
burundi/waterfalls.alt: the Karera falls dropping through forest in southern Burundi

burundi/why-visit.caption: Why Burundi
burundi/why-visit.description: The Nile's furthest source, the royal drums, and a lake almost nobody visits.
burundi/why-visit.alt: a fishing boat on Lake Tanganyika below green hills, Burundi

burundi/wildlife.caption: Chimpanzees at Kibira
burundi/wildlife.description: Montane forest continuous with Rwanda's Nyungwe, with chimpanzee and colobus in it.
burundi/wildlife.alt: a chimpanzee in the montane forest canopy at Kibira, Burundi

cabo-verde/adventure.caption: Kitesurfing and Ridge Walking
cabo-verde/adventure.description: Sal and Boa Vista for wind, and Santo Antao for some of the best walking in the Atlantic.
cabo-verde/adventure.alt: a kitesurfer in strong wind off Sal, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/architecture.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Volcanic Stone
cabo-verde/architecture.description: Pastel colonial in Mindelo, and black volcanic stone houses on Fogo.
cabo-verde/architecture.alt: black volcanic stone houses inside the Fogo caldera, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/beaches.caption: Sal, Boa Vista and Tarrafal
cabo-verde/beaches.description: White sand and constant wind on Sal and Boa Vista, and quiet bays on Santiago.
cabo-verde/beaches.alt: windsurfers and white sand on a beach at Sal, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/cities.caption: Praia and Mindelo
cabo-verde/cities.description: A clifftop capital on Santiago, and the port city on Sao Vicente where the music lives.
cabo-verde/cities.alt: the harbour and colonial buildings of Mindelo, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/crafts.caption: Pottery, Panu and Grogue
cabo-verde/crafts.description: The panu woven cloth of Santiago, Fogo's pottery, and cane spirit stills.
cabo-verde/crafts.alt: a woven panu cloth on a narrow Cabo Verdean loom

cabo-verde/culture.caption: Creole, and the Morna
cabo-verde/culture.description: A Portuguese-African creole culture, and a music that put these islands on the map.
cabo-verde/culture.alt: a morna band playing in a small bar in Mindelo, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/eco-tourism.caption: Turtle Patrols on Boa Vista
cabo-verde/eco-tourism.description: Community and NGO patrols on the nesting beaches, and the numbers have recovered.
cabo-verde/eco-tourism.alt: volunteers recording a turtle nest at night on Boa Vista, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/family-community.caption: Beaches and Short Flights
cabo-verde/family-community.description: Calm water on Sal and Boa Vista, short hops between islands, and a very easy pace.
cabo-verde/family-community.alt: children playing in calm shallow water on a Cabo Verde beach

cabo-verde/festivals.caption: Mindelo Carnival and Baia das Gatas
cabo-verde/festivals.description: Carnival in February and a music festival on the beach in August.
cabo-verde/festivals.alt: carnival costumes and crowds in the streets of Mindelo, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/food.caption: Cachupa and Grogue
cabo-verde/food.description: Cachupa — the slow-cooked maize and bean stew — and grogue distilled from cane.
cabo-verde/food.alt: a bowl of cachupa with sausage and egg, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/forests.caption: The Cloud Forest of Santo Antao
cabo-verde/forests.description: The north of Santo Antao catches enough cloud to grow coffee and dragon trees.
cabo-verde/forests.alt: dragon trees and cloud in the highlands of Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/heritage.caption: Cidade Velha, Listed
cabo-verde/heritage.description: Inscribed in 2009 — the pillory, the cathedral ruins and the street plan of the first town.
cabo-verde/heritage.alt: the stone pillory in the square at Cidade Velha, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/hero.caption: Fogo
cabo-verde/hero.description: A 2,829-metre volcano with a village and vineyards inside its caldera, and it erupts.
cabo-verde/hero.alt: the cone of Pico do Fogo rising inside its caldera, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/hidden-gems.caption: Brava
cabo-verde/hidden-gems.description: The smallest inhabited island, reached only by boat, with flowers and no airport worth the name.
cabo-verde/hidden-gems.alt: the green terraced slopes and village of Brava island, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/historic-sites.caption: Cidade Velha
cabo-verde/historic-sites.description: The first European colonial town in the tropics, founded in 1462, with the fort above it.
cabo-verde/historic-sites.alt: the church and fort ruins at Cidade Velha on Santiago, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/lakes-rivers.caption: Ribeiras
cabo-verde/lakes-rivers.description: Steep valleys terraced for sugarcane and coffee, and irrigated by hand-cut channels.
cabo-verde/lakes-rivers.alt: terraced sugarcane and levada channels in a Santo Antao ribeira, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/local-life.caption: The Bar at Midnight
cabo-verde/local-life.description: Mindelo's bars start late and the morna does not begin until they are full.
cabo-verde/local-life.alt: a late-night bar in Mindelo with musicians playing, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/luxury.caption: Well Established
cabo-verde/luxury.description: Resorts on Sal and Boa Vista, and small good hotels on Santo Antao and Fogo.
cabo-verde/luxury.alt: a small hotel terrace above the sea on Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/mountains.caption: Pico do Fogo and Santo Antao
cabo-verde/mountains.description: Fogo's cone, and Santo Antao's ridges where the paths run along the crest.
cabo-verde/mountains.alt: a cobbled path running along a knife-edge ridge on Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/nature.caption: Ten Islands, Ten Climates
cabo-verde/nature.description: Desert dunes on Boa Vista and cloud forest on Santo Antao, in the same archipelago.
cabo-verde/nature.alt: terraced green ribeiras cutting into the mountains of Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/outdoor.caption: Walking Santo Antao
cabo-verde/outdoor.description: Cobbled paths from the ridge down to the sea, a day at a time, between villages.
cabo-verde/outdoor.alt: walkers descending a cobbled path towards the sea on Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/photography.caption: Volcano and Vine
cabo-verde/photography.description: Cha das Caldeiras at first light, with vines growing in black ash under the cone.
cabo-verde/photography.alt: vineyards in black volcanic ash below the cone of Fogo, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/safari.caption: Sea, Not Savanna
cabo-verde/safari.description: No large land animals. What there is instead is turtles, whales and seabirds.
cabo-verde/safari.alt: a humpback whale off the Cabo Verdean coast

cabo-verde/traditional-people.caption: The Badiu and the Sampadjudu
cabo-verde/traditional-people.description: The Santiago interior and the northern islands, with different histories and different music.
cabo-verde/traditional-people.alt: musicians playing batuko drums on Santiago, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/waterfalls.caption: Seasonal Only
cabo-verde/waterfalls.description: The rain comes in August and September, and the ribeiras run for a few weeks.
cabo-verde/waterfalls.alt: a dry stone-walled ribeira valley on Santo Antao, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/why-visit.caption: Why Cabo Verde
cabo-verde/why-visit.description: An active volcano with vineyards in it, ridge walking above the Atlantic, and the morna.
cabo-verde/why-visit.alt: the cone of Fogo above black lava and white houses, Cabo Verde

cabo-verde/wildlife.caption: Turtles and Humpbacks
cabo-verde/wildlife.description: Boa Vista is one of the largest loggerhead nesting sites in the world.
cabo-verde/wildlife.alt: a loggerhead turtle returning to the sea on Boa Vista, Cabo Verde

cameroon/adventure.caption: Summit, Crater, Coast
cameroon/adventure.description: The Guinness route to 4,095 m, down the north flank to Mann's Spring, and out to the sea on the same trip.
cameroon/adventure.alt: walkers crossing grass slopes below the summit huts on Mount Cameroon

cameroon/architecture.caption: Chefferie and Colonial Buea
cameroon/architecture.description: Bamileke chefferie compounds with carved posts and conical roofs, and the German Schloss on the hill above Buea.
cameroon/architecture.alt: a Bamileke chieftaincy compound with carved posts and a conical thatched roof, Cameroon

cameroon/beaches.caption: Black Sand and Warm Water
cameroon/beaches.description: Volcanic grey-black sand at Limbe, white sand and fishing pirogues at Kribi, warm all year on both.
cameroon/beaches.alt: surf breaking on volcanic black sand at dusk on the Cameroon coast near Limbe

cameroon/cities.caption: Douala and Yaounde
cameroon/cities.description: The port that moves the country and the hill capital that governs it, ninety minutes apart by air and nothing alike.
cameroon/cities.alt: a street in the Bonapriso quarter of Douala, Cameroon

cameroon/crafts.caption: The Foumban Bronze Casters
cameroon/crafts.description: Lost-wax bronze, beaded thrones and carved masks made on the craft street the same way they were three centuries ago.
cameroon/crafts.alt: a bronze caster working molten metal in a workshop at Foumban, Cameroon

cameroon/culture.caption: The Grassfields Kingdoms
cameroon/culture.description: Bamileke and Bamoun chiefdoms in the west, still functioning, with palaces, secret societies and their own calendars.
cameroon/culture.alt: a carved and beaded royal throne inside a palace museum at Foumban, Cameroon

cameroon/eco-tourism.query: Cameroon forest guide identifying tree species inside ecotourism conservation
cameroon/eco-tourism.alt: a forest guide identifying a tree species inside Korup rainforest, Cameroon

cameroon/family-community.caption: Village and Mountain Together
cameroon/family-community.description: Guides and porters come from the mountain villages in rotation, and the trail money goes back into the village fund.
cameroon/family-community.alt: villagers and guides repairing a stone section of mountain trail together, Cameroon

cameroon/festivals.query: Cameroon masked dancers horsemen nguon festival foumban celebration dance
cameroon/festivals.alt: masked dancers and horsemen at the Nguon festival in Foumban, Cameroon

cameroon/food.caption: Ndole, Poulet DG and Grilled Fish
cameroon/food.description: Bitterleaf and groundnut ndolé, plantain, and whole fish grilled on the sand at Kribi within sight of the boat.
cameroon/food.alt: grilled fish and plantain served at a beachside stall in Kribi, Cameroon

cameroon/forests.caption: Inside Korup
cameroon/forests.description: One of the oldest rainforests in Africa, with a canopy suspension bridge over the Mana river and 400 tree species.
cameroon/forests.alt: a canopy suspension bridge over a river inside Korup rainforest, Cameroon

cameroon/heritage.caption: Dja, Rhumsiki and the Mandara
cameroon/heritage.description: The Dja Faunal Reserve is UNESCO World Heritage; the volcanic spires above Rhumsiki are the image on the old banknote.
cameroon/heritage.alt: volcanic rock spires rising from farmland at Rhumsiki in the Mandara mountains, Cameroon

cameroon/hero.query: Cameroon upper slopes mount cameroon above atlantic landscape iconic
cameroon/hero.alt: the upper slopes of Mount Cameroon at dawn above the Atlantic

cameroon/hidden-gems.caption: The 1999 Lava Fields
cameroon/hidden-gems.description: Black lava tongues from the 1999 and 2000 flows running down to the sea near Bakingili, with green already coming back.
cameroon/hidden-gems.alt: black solidified lava flows reaching the sea on the flank of Mount Cameroon

cameroon/historic-sites.caption: The Sultan's Palace
cameroon/historic-sites.description: The 1917 palace at Foumban and its museum of the Bamoun kings, plus the German colonial buildings still standing in Buea.
cameroon/historic-sites.alt: the Sultan's Palace at Foumban with its museum of the Bamoun kings, Cameroon

cameroon/lakes-rivers.query: Cameroon brown benoue river gallery forest along lake water
cameroon/lakes-rivers.alt: the wide brown Benoue river with gallery forest along the bank, Cameroon

cameroon/local-life.caption: Marche Central, Motos, Rain
cameroon/local-life.description: Bilingual, loud and unbothered: Douala's markets, the moto-taxis, and the sudden rain everyone waits out under an awning.
cameroon/local-life.alt: traders and moto-taxis in a busy Douala market street, Cameroon

cameroon/luxury.caption: Kribi, Slowly
cameroon/luxury.description: Small beach hotels south of Kribi, a driver who knows the road, and nothing at all scheduled after lunch.
cameroon/luxury.alt: a small beach hotel terrace above the sand at Kribi, Cameroon

cameroon/mountains.alt: trekkers on the open upper slopes of Mount Cameroon above the tree line

cameroon/outdoor.caption: The Ring Road on Foot
cameroon/outdoor.description: Crater lakes, tea slopes and the Ring Road through the Bamenda highlands, walkable in sections between 1,200 and 2,000 m.
cameroon/outdoor.alt: open dry-season slopes and ridge lines on Mount Cameroon

cameroon/photography.caption: Cloud on the Rainforest
cameroon/photography.description: Wet season cloud sitting on the forest above Buea, and dry season light on the Mandara spires — two countries, one lens.
cameroon/photography.alt: cloud and rain sitting on the rainforest above Buea, Cameroon

cameroon/safari.query: Cameroon elephants giraffe dry season waterhole waza safari game drive
cameroon/safari.alt: elephants and giraffe at a dry-season waterhole in Waza National Park, Cameroon

cameroon/traditional-people.caption: Fulani, Mafa and Bamileke
cameroon/traditional-people.description: Two hundred and fifty ethnic groups and as many languages, from the Mafa terraces of the Mandara to the Fulani of the Sahel.
cameroon/traditional-people.alt: a Mafa farmer on the terraced slopes of the Mandara mountains, Cameroon

cameroon/waterfalls.caption: Where the River Meets the Sea
cameroon/waterfalls.description: The Lobé falls near Kribi drop straight over black rock into the Atlantic — one of very few waterfalls on earth that do.
cameroon/waterfalls.alt: the Lobe waterfalls pouring over rock directly into the Atlantic near Kribi, Cameroon

cameroon/why-visit.caption: Everything, Within One Border
cameroon/why-visit.description: Sea level to Sahel in nine hundred kilometres, French and English on the same road, and almost nobody else on it.
cameroon/why-visit.alt: a 4x4 on a red laterite road between rainforest and highland farmland, Cameroon

cameroon/wildlife.alt: forest elephants among buttressed trees in Korup National Park, Cameroon

central-african-republic/adventure.caption: Tracking on Foot
central-african-republic/adventure.description: Gorillas in the morning, the bai in the afternoon, and net-hunting with the BaAka between.
central-african-republic/adventure.alt: trackers moving quietly through dense forest undergrowth, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/adventure.query: Central African Republic trackers moving quietly

central-african-republic/architecture.caption: Colonial and Forest Camp
central-african-republic/architecture.description: French colonial in Bangui, and leaf-and-sapling mongulu shelters in the forest.
central-african-republic/architecture.alt: a domed leaf mongulu shelter in a BaAka forest camp, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/beaches.caption: River Sand
central-african-republic/beaches.description: Landlocked. The sandbanks on the Sangha come out in the dry season and people use them.
central-african-republic/beaches.alt: a wide sandbank on the Sangha river in the dry season, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/beaches.query: Central African Republic sandbank sangha river

central-african-republic/cities.caption: Bangui
central-african-republic/cities.description: On the Ubangi, opposite the Congo, with the Marche Central at the middle of it.
central-african-republic/cities.alt: the Ubangi riverfront and market at Bangui, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/crafts.caption: Nets, Baskets and Bark Cloth
central-african-republic/crafts.description: Hunting nets woven from forest liana, and bark cloth beaten from tree fibre.
central-african-republic/crafts.alt: a woven forest hunting net and bark cloth, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/crafts.query: Central African Republic woven forest hunting

central-african-republic/culture.caption: The BaAka
central-african-republic/culture.description: Forest hunter-gatherers whose polyphonic singing is on the UNESCO intangible list.
central-african-republic/culture.alt: BaAka women singing in polyphony in a forest camp, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/eco-tourism.caption: Dzanga-Sangha's Model
central-african-republic/eco-tourism.description: The reserve employs BaAka trackers and shares gate revenue with the villages around it.
central-african-republic/eco-tourism.alt: Eco Tourism in Central African Republic

central-african-republic/family-communit.caption: Not Yet
central-african-republic/family-communit.description: This is expedition travel in a country with a hard recent history, and it is not for families.
central-african-republic/family-communit.alt: a village school in a forest clearing, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/family-communit.query: Central African Republic village school forest

central-african-republic/festivals.caption: BaAka Polyphony
central-african-republic/festivals.description: Sung in overlapping parts, with no leader and no fixed melody, and it has been studied by composers for fifty years.
central-african-republic/festivals.alt: BaAka singers and drummers around a forest camp fire, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/festivals.query: Central African Republic baaka singers drummers

central-african-republic/food.caption: Cassava, Bushmeat and Palm Wine
central-african-republic/food.description: Cassava as the staple, smoked fish from the river, and palm wine tapped in the forest.
central-african-republic/food.alt: smoked river fish and cassava on a plate, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/food.query: Central African Republic smoked river fish

central-african-republic/forests.caption: Dzanga-Sangha
central-african-republic/forests.description: Old-growth Congo Basin forest, shared with Cameroon and Congo as a trinational park.
central-african-republic/forests.alt: buttressed rainforest giants in Dzanga-Sangha, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/heritage.caption: Two Sites
central-african-republic/heritage.description: Dzanga-Sangha for its forest, and Manovo-Gounda St Floris in the north, on the danger list.
central-african-republic/heritage.alt: open savanna and gallery forest in northern CAR, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/hero.caption: Dzanga Bai
central-african-republic/hero.description: A mineral clearing in the forest where a hundred elephants gather in an afternoon.
central-african-republic/hero.alt: forest elephants gathered at the Dzanga Bai clearing, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/hidden-gems.caption: Chimpanzees at Bai Hokou
central-african-republic/hidden-gems.description: A second habituated group, and the walk in is as good as the sighting.
central-african-republic/hidden-gems.alt: a chimpanzee resting in a forest tree at Bai Hokou, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/historic-sites.caption: Bangui's Colonial Quarter
central-african-republic/historic-sites.description: A river capital laid out by the French, and much of it still standing.
central-african-republic/historic-sites.alt: a colonial-era building on the riverfront at Bangui, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/historic-sites.query: Central African Republic colonial era building

central-african-republic/lakes-rivers.caption: The Sangha and the Ubangi
central-african-republic/lakes-rivers.description: The Sangha runs down to the Congo; the Ubangi is the whole southern border.
central-african-republic/lakes-rivers.alt: the Sangha river running between walls of rainforest, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/local-life.caption: The Marche Central
central-african-republic/local-life.description: Everything from cassava to river fish, and the noise of a city that never stops trading.
central-african-republic/local-life.alt: crowds and stalls at the Marche Central in Bangui, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/local-life.query: Central African Republic Marche Central Bangui

central-african-republic/luxury.caption: One Lodge
central-african-republic/luxury.description: Sangha Lodge at Dzanga-Sangha, and nothing comparable anywhere else in the country.
central-african-republic/luxury.alt: a forest lodge deck overlooking the Sangha river, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/luxury.query: Central African Republic forest lodge deck

central-african-republic/mountains.caption: The Fertit Hills and Mont Ngaoui
central-african-republic/mountains.description: 1,420 metres on the Cameroon border, in country almost nobody visits.
central-african-republic/mountains.alt: wooded hills rising above savanna in western CAR, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/nature.caption: The Congo Basin Forest
central-african-republic/nature.description: The northern edge of the second largest rainforest on earth, and it starts here.
central-african-republic/nature.alt: unbroken rainforest canopy in the Dzanga-Sangha reserve, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/outdoor.caption: Forest Walking
central-african-republic/outdoor.description: Everything here is done on foot, quietly, behind a tracker.
central-african-republic/outdoor.alt: a narrow trail through dense Congo Basin forest, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/photography.caption: Elephants in a Clearing
central-african-republic/photography.description: Dzanga Bai from the platform at four in the afternoon, when the light comes in sideways.
central-african-republic/photography.alt: afternoon light across forest elephants at Dzanga Bai, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/photography.query: Central African Republic forest elephants dzanga

central-african-republic/safari.caption: Forest, Not Savanna
central-african-republic/safari.description: This is bai-watching and forest tracking. Bongo, forest buffalo and sitatunga, all on foot.
central-african-republic/safari.alt: a bongo antelope at the edge of a forest clearing, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/safari.query: Central African Republic bongo antelope edge

central-african-republic/traditional-peo.caption: BaAka and Sangha-Sangha
central-african-republic/traditional-peo.description: The BaAka in the forest, and the Sangha-Sangha along the river.
central-african-republic/traditional-peo.alt: a BaAka net-hunting party moving through forest, Central African Republic

central-african-republic/waterfalls.caption: Boali
central-african-republic/waterfalls.description: Fifty metres of water on the M'Bali river, two hours from Bangui.
central-african-republic/waterfalls.alt: the Boali waterfall dropping over a wide ledge, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/waterfalls.query: Central African Republic boali waterfall dropping

central-african-republic/why-visit.caption: Why the Central African Republic
central-african-republic/why-visit.description: A hundred forest elephants in one clearing, watched from a platform, by almost no one.
central-african-republic/why-visit.alt: a viewing platform overlooking elephants at a forest bai, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/why-visit.query: Central African Republic viewing platform overlooking

central-african-republic/wildlife.caption: Western Lowland Gorillas
central-african-republic/wildlife.description: Habituated groups tracked on foot, with far fewer visitors than in the east.
central-african-republic/wildlife.alt: a western lowland gorilla in forest undergrowth, Central African Republic
central-african-republic/wildlife.query: Central African Republic western lowland gorilla

chad/adventure.caption: Crossing the Ennedi
chad/adventure.description: Ten days by four-wheel-drive between arches and gueltas, sleeping under the rock.
chad/adventure.alt: a desert camp under a sandstone arch in the Ennedi, Chad

chad/architecture.caption: Mud and Banco
chad/architecture.description: Sahelian mud-brick in the towns, and reed and mat construction on the lake.
chad/architecture.alt: a mud-brick compound with a thatched granary in the Sahel, Chad

chad/beaches.caption: Landlocked, and the Lake
chad/beaches.description: The beaches here are the shores of Lake Chad, worked by fishermen in reed boats.
chad/beaches.alt: reed fishing boats on the shore of Lake Chad

chad/cities.caption: N'Djamena
chad/cities.description: A capital on the Chari, opposite Cameroon, with the largest market in the region.
chad/cities.alt: the riverfront and low skyline of N'Djamena on the Chari, Chad

chad/crafts.caption: Leatherwork and Silver
chad/crafts.description: Toubou leather, Sara basketry, and silver from the N'Djamena market.
chad/crafts.alt: tooled leather camel gear and silver at a Chadian market

chad/culture.caption: Two Hundred Groups
chad/culture.description: Toubou and Zaghawa in the north, Sara in the south, and Arabic and French across both.
chad/culture.alt: a market crowd in N'Djamena, Chad

chad/eco-tourism.caption: The Turnaround at Zakouma
chad/eco-tourism.description: African Parks took it on in 2010 after poaching had taken ninety per cent of the elephants.
chad/eco-tourism.alt: a ranger patrol vehicle at dawn in Zakouma, Chad

chad/family-community.caption: Serious Country
chad/family-community.description: Distances are enormous and facilities are few. Zakouma is possible; the Ennedi is an expedition.
chad/family-community.alt: a vehicle on a long empty track across Chadian savanna

chad/festivals.caption: The Gerewol and the Camel Races
chad/festivals.description: Wodaabe gatherings in the Sahel, and camel racing in the desert north.
chad/festivals.alt: camel racing at a gathering in the Chadian Sahel

chad/food.caption: Boule and Grilled Capitaine
chad/food.description: Millet boule with sauce, and Nile perch off the Chari grilled on the bank.
chad/food.alt: grilled capitaine fish and millet boule on a plate, Chad

chad/forests.caption: Gallery Forest on the Rivers
chad/forests.description: The Chari and Logone carry woodland far north into the Sahel.
chad/forests.alt: gallery forest along the Chari river in southern Chad

chad/heritage.caption: Two Sites in the Sahara
chad/heritage.description: The Ennedi massif and the Ounianga lakes, both World Heritage, both barely visited.
chad/heritage.alt: the layered sandstone towers of the Ennedi at sunset, Chad

chad/hero.caption: Zakouma
chad/hero.description: One of Africa's great turnarounds: from four hundred and fifty elephants to over six hundred.
chad/hero.alt: a large herd of elephants moving across floodplain in Zakouma, Chad

chad/hidden-gems.caption: The Guelta d'Archei
chad/hidden-gems.description: Camels come down a gorge to drink, and desert crocodiles live in the pool below them.
chad/hidden-gems.alt: camels descending to the dark water of the Guelta d'Archei, Chad

chad/historic-sites.caption: Ennedi Rock Art
chad/historic-sites.description: Thousands of painted and engraved panels recording a Sahara with cattle and giraffe in it.
chad/historic-sites.alt: painted rock art figures of cattle on Ennedi sandstone, Chad

chad/lakes-rivers.caption: Lake Chad and the Ounianga Lakes
chad/lakes-rivers.description: A shrinking inland sea in the west, and eighteen lakes in the Sahara that no river feeds.
chad/lakes-rivers.alt: the blue and green lakes of Ounianga between dunes, Chad

chad/local-life.caption: Tea in the Shade
chad/local-life.description: Three glasses, poured from a height, and no business concluded before the third.
chad/local-life.alt: men drinking tea in the shade of a wall in N'Djamena, Chad

chad/luxury.caption: One Camp, and It Is Good
chad/luxury.description: Zakouma has a single seasonal camp. The Ennedi is tents you bring with you.
chad/luxury.alt: a seasonal tented camp under trees in Zakouma, Chad

chad/mountains.caption: Emi Koussi and the Tibesti
chad/mountains.description: A 3,415-metre volcano in the far north, the highest point in the Sahara.
chad/mountains.alt: the volcanic massif of the Tibesti rising from desert, Chad

chad/nature.caption: The Ennedi
chad/nature.description: A sandstone massif eroded into arches, towers and canyons, with water at the bottom of them.
chad/nature.alt: the Aloba arch standing over sand in the Ennedi massif, Chad

chad/outdoor.caption: Walking Zakouma
chad/outdoor.description: Zakouma allows walking with armed rangers, which very few West and Central African parks do.
chad/outdoor.alt: a walking group with a ranger among trees in Zakouma, Chad

chad/photography.caption: Sandstone and Shadow
chad/photography.description: The Ennedi arches in the last hour, when the sandstone goes from orange to red.
chad/photography.alt: low sun through a sandstone arch in the Ennedi, Chad

chad/safari.caption: Zakouma in March
chad/safari.description: Everything concentrates on the last pans, and the birdlife with it — crowned crane in their thousands.
chad/safari.alt: black crowned cranes gathered at a drying pan in Zakouma, Chad

chad/traditional-people.caption: The Toubou
chad/traditional-people.description: A desert people of the Tibesti and Ennedi, and among the most self-sufficient anywhere.
chad/traditional-people.alt: a Toubou man beside camels in the Ennedi, Chad

chad/waterfalls.caption: None, and Guelta Instead
chad/waterfalls.description: No falls. What the Ennedi has is the Guelta d'Archei, a permanent gorge pool.
chad/waterfalls.alt: camels drinking at the Guelta d'Archei gorge pool, Chad

chad/why-visit.caption: Why Chad
chad/why-visit.description: A national park that came back from the dead, and a desert massif almost nobody has seen.
chad/why-visit.alt: a lone vehicle beneath the vast sandstone towers of the Ennedi, Chad

chad/wildlife.caption: Buffalo in Thousands
chad/wildlife.description: Zakouma's buffalo move in herds of over a thousand, and the Kordofan giraffe with them.
chad/wildlife.alt: a dense herd of buffalo raising dust in Zakouma, Chad

comoros/adventure.caption: Climbing Karthala
comoros/adventure.description: Overnight from Boboni, camping on the rim, and down the next day.
comoros/adventure.alt: walkers camping on the crater rim of Karthala, Comoros

comoros/architecture.caption: Swahili Stone
comoros/architecture.description: Coral-stone houses with carved doors, and the mosque architecture of the whole coast.
comoros/architecture.alt: a carved wooden Swahili door in a coral-stone wall, Comoros

comoros/beaches.caption: Black Sand and White
comoros/beaches.description: Black volcanic sand on Grande Comore, and white on Moheli and Anjouan.
comoros/beaches.alt: black volcanic sand and clear water on a Grande Comore beach, Comoros

comoros/cities.caption: Moroni and Mutsamudu
comoros/cities.description: A volcanic harbour capital, and Anjouan's stone town under a citadel.
comoros/cities.alt: the stone town and citadel of Mutsamudu on Anjouan, Comoros

comoros/crafts.caption: Woodwork, Gold and Embroidery
comoros/crafts.description: Carved doors, gold wedding jewellery, and the embroidered kofia cap.
comoros/crafts.alt: an embroidered Comorian kofia cap and carved door detail, Comoros

comoros/culture.caption: Swahili, and Ylang-Ylang
comoros/culture.description: A Swahili island culture, and most of the world's ylang-ylang for perfume.
comoros/culture.alt: ylang-ylang flowers being picked on a Comorian plantation, Comoros

comoros/eco-tourism.caption: Moheli's Community Park
comoros/eco-tourism.description: The marine park is run with the villages, and the turtle numbers have held because of it.
comoros/eco-tourism.alt: a community ranger recording turtle nests on Moheli, Comoros

comoros/family-community.caption: Turtles and Shallow Reef
comoros/family-community.description: Moheli's nesting beaches, and reef close enough in to snorkel from the sand.
comoros/family-community.alt: children snorkelling over shallow reef off a Comorian beach, Comoros

comoros/festivals.caption: The Grand Mariage Season
comoros/festivals.description: Weddings run through the dry season and take over whole villages for days.
comoros/festivals.alt: a village square during a Grand Mariage celebration, Comoros

comoros/food.caption: Langouste and Pilao
comoros/food.description: Lobster off the reef, pilao rice with cardamom, and vanilla and clove in everything.
comoros/food.alt: grilled lobster with rice and coconut sauce, Comoros

comoros/forests.caption: The Last Forest
comoros/forests.description: Karthala's forest, and Moheli's, hold the bats, the flying fox and the endemic birds.
comoros/forests.alt: cloud forest on the slopes of Mount Karthala, Comoros

comoros/heritage.caption: Nothing Listed, Much Standing
comoros/heritage.description: No World Heritage sites, and Swahili stone towns on all three islands.
comoros/heritage.alt: narrow stone alleys in the medina of Moroni, Comoros

comoros/hero.caption: Karthala
comoros/hero.description: An active volcano with one of the largest craters on earth, walked up overnight.
comoros/hero.alt: the vast summit crater of Mount Karthala on Grande Comore, Comoros

comoros/hidden-gems.caption: The Coelacanth
comoros/hidden-gems.description: Caught off these islands in 1938, having been extinct for eighty million years.
comoros/hidden-gems.alt: a preserved coelacanth specimen in a Comorian museum case, Comoros

comoros/historic-sites.caption: The Medina of Moroni
comoros/historic-sites.description: A Swahili stone town with the Old Friday Mosque on the harbour since 1427.
comoros/historic-sites.alt: the Old Friday Mosque on the harbour at Moroni, Comoros

comoros/lakes-rivers.caption: No Rivers on Grande Comore
comoros/lakes-rivers.description: The lava is too porous to hold a river — the water is in cisterns and Lake Sale.
comoros/lakes-rivers.alt: the crater lake of Lac Sale beside the sea on Grande Comore, Comoros

comoros/local-life.caption: The Harbour at Moroni
comoros/local-life.description: Dhows unloading onto the rocks, and the mosque directly behind them.
comoros/local-life.alt: dhows unloading at the rocky harbour below Moroni's mosque, Comoros

comoros/luxury.caption: Small and Simple
comoros/luxury.description: Guesthouses and a few beach hotels. Nothing at the top end anywhere.
comoros/luxury.alt: a small beach guesthouse under palms on Moheli, Comoros

comoros/mountains.caption: The Volcanic Interior
comoros/mountains.description: Karthala at 2,361 metres on Grande Comore, and Ntringui on Anjouan.
comoros/mountains.alt: the forested volcanic interior of Anjouan, Comoros

comoros/nature.caption: Three Islands and a Claim
comoros/nature.description: Grande Comore, Anjouan and Moheli, each volcanic, each different, and Mayotte disputed.
comoros/nature.alt: the volcanic coastline and black rock of Grande Comore, Comoros

comoros/outdoor.caption: Volcano and Reef
comoros/outdoor.description: Karthala overnight, and diving the drop-offs on the same trip.
comoros/outdoor.alt: a diver over a coral drop-off in Comorian water, Comoros

comoros/photography.caption: Volcano and Ocean
comoros/photography.description: Karthala's rim at first light, with the Indian Ocean on every side of it.
comoros/photography.alt: sunrise from the crater rim of Karthala over the ocean, Comoros

comoros/safari.caption: Moheli Marine Park
comoros/safari.description: Turtles nesting in numbers, dugong, and humpbacks calving between July and October.
comoros/safari.alt: a green turtle coming ashore on a Moheli beach at night, Comoros

comoros/traditional-people.caption: The Grand Mariage
comoros/traditional-people.description: The anda — a marriage that confers social rank, and can take a decade to afford.
comoros/traditional-people.alt: a Grand Mariage procession with drummers and gold jewellery, Comoros

comoros/waterfalls.caption: Anjouan's Cascades
comoros/waterfalls.description: The Dziancoundre falls, and streams off the interior that run all year.
comoros/waterfalls.alt: a waterfall falling through forest into a pool on Anjouan, Comoros

comoros/why-visit.caption: Why Comoros
comoros/why-visit.description: An active volcano, a living fossil, and a Swahili stone town nobody visits.
comoros/why-visit.alt: a dhow off the volcanic coast of Grande Comore at sunset, Comoros

comoros/wildlife.caption: Livingstone's Fruit Bat
comoros/wildlife.description: A metre and a half across, found on Anjouan and Moheli and nowhere else.
comoros/wildlife.alt: a Livingstone's fruit bat hanging in forest canopy on Anjouan, Comoros

congo/adventure.caption: Forest and River
congo/adventure.description: Pirogue on the Lekoli, tracking on foot, and nights on a bai platform.
congo/adventure.alt: a pirogue moving up a narrow forest river in Odzala, Congo

congo/beaches.caption: A Hundred and Seventy Kilometres of Atlantic
congo/beaches.description: Pointe-Noire's beaches, and the empty sand of the Conkouati coast north of it.
congo/beaches.alt: an empty Atlantic beach backed by forest at Conkouati, Congo

congo/culture.caption: Congolese Rumba
congo/culture.description: Rumba was made on both banks of this river, and it is on the UNESCO list because of it.
congo/culture.alt: a rumba band performing at a bar in Brazzaville, Congo

congo/festivals.caption: The Feux de Brazza
congo/festivals.description: A music festival in Brazzaville, and rumba the rest of the year in every bar.
congo/festivals.alt: a crowd dancing at a music festival in Brazzaville, Congo

congo/food.caption: Saka-Saka and Poulet Moambe
congo/food.description: Cassava leaf, and chicken in palm nut sauce — the dish of both Congos.
congo/food.alt: a plate of poulet moambe with cassava and rice, Congo

congo/forests.caption: Nouabale-Ndoki
congo/forests.description: Forest that has never been logged, and the Goualougo Triangle where the chimps had not seen people.
congo/forests.alt: old-growth rainforest with enormous buttressed trees at Ndoki, Congo

congo/hero.caption: Odzala-Kokoua
congo/hero.description: Forest, savanna and bais together, and gorillas habituated for tracking on foot.
congo/hero.alt: a forest bai clearing surrounded by rainforest in Odzala, Congo

congo/lakes-rivers.caption: The Congo River
congo/lakes-rivers.description: The second largest river on earth by volume, and the whole eastern border of the country.
congo/lakes-rivers.alt: the vast brown Congo river with forest on the far bank

congo/mountains.caption: Mount Berongou
congo/mountains.description: 903 metres in the Mayombe, and the highest ground in a country of forest and plateau.
congo/mountains.alt: the forested Mayombe hills under low cloud, Congo

congo/nature.caption: The Congo Basin
congo/nature.description: Two thirds of the country is rainforest, and much of it has never had a road in it.
congo/nature.alt: unbroken Congo Basin rainforest canopy from the air

congo/safari.caption: Bai Watching
congo/safari.description: Forest buffalo, bongo, sitatunga and elephant come to the clearings, and you sit and wait.
congo/safari.alt: forest buffalo and elephants at a bai in Odzala, Congo

congo/traditional-people.caption: Kongo, Teke, Mbochi and the Aka
congo/traditional-people.description: Bantu peoples along the river, and Aka forest hunter-gatherers in the north.
congo/traditional-people.alt: an Aka forest camp with leaf shelters in the north, Congo

congo/waterfalls.caption: The Loufoulakari
congo/waterfalls.description: Falls on the Congo above Brazzaville, where the river drops through rock.
congo/waterfalls.alt: the Loufoulakari falls dropping through rock into the Congo

congo/wildlife.caption: Western Lowland Gorillas
congo/wildlife.description: Smaller, redder and harder to see than mountain gorillas, and tracked through swamp forest.
congo/wildlife.alt: a silverback western lowland gorilla in dense green forest, Congo

cote-divoire/adventure.caption: Surf, Hike, Paddle
cote-divoire/adventure.description: Surf at Assinie, hiking the western hills, and pirogues through the lagoon.
cote-divoire/adventure.alt: surfers in the water off Assinie, Côte d'Ivoire

cote-divoire/architecture.caption: Lagoon Colonial
